literal: One should choose a great general whom the Hu obey and trust, take several hundred horsemen, go to take command of Biao's army and subdue them — when the bandits hear of it they will surely quake at the wind.
idiomatic: Pick a great general the Hu fear and obey, give him a few hundred riders, and send him to take Biao's army in hand — when the bandits hear of it they will break at the mere rumor.

literal: Marquis of Shouguang Jian, formerly in Bingzhou, was famed as fierce and martial; the Hu feared and submitted to him, and no general could match him.
idiomatic: Marquis of Shouguang Sun Jian had once held Bingzhou, famed as fierce and martial; the Hu feared him and bowed, and no general could stand beside him.

literal: " Taizong followed this and thereupon pacified the Hu raiders.
idiomatic: " Taizong took his counsel and pacified the Hu raiders.

literal: Soon he was appointed Chief of the Celestial Department and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: Soon he was made chief of the celestial department and raised to duke.

literal: In summer of the third year of Taichang, Xuanbo's illness grew grave; Taizong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Duke of Yidu Mu Guan to receive his last words, and again sent court attendants to inquire after his health — several times in one night.
idiomatic: In the third year of Taichang, summer, Xuanbo's illness turned grave; Taizong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Duke of Yidu Mu Guan to take his last words and sent court attendants to ask after him again and again through the night.

literal: When he died, an edict mourned him deeply; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and titled Duke Wenzhen.
idiomatic: When he died, the throne mourned him in edict, posthumously made him minister of works, and titled him Duke Wenzhen.

literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.
idiomatic: His funeral followed wholly the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

literal: An edict ordered all ministers and attached-state chieftains to attend the burial; except for princes of the blood, all were made to bow and escort.
idiomatic: An edict gathered every minister and attached-state chieftain to the burial; save for princes of the blood, all were made to bow and escort the bier.

literal: In the Taihe era, Emperor Gaozu, recording meritorious ministers of the former court, had Xuanbo receive joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era Emperor Gaozu, recording ministers of the former court, had Xuanbo given joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.

literal: Unless for court documents of the throne or letters to the four directions, Xuanbo never touched the brush — hence no writings survive in the world.
idiomatic: Unless for court edicts or letters to the four quarters, Xuanbo never took up the brush — and so no writings of his survive.

literal: He was especially skilled in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script — models for the age.
idiomatic: He excelled above all in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script, and the age copied him as its model.

literal: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang Lu Chen were both famed for broad arts.
idiomatic: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were both famed for wide learning in the arts.

literal: Chen learned from Zhong You, Yue from Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive — each attaining the utmost subtlety.
idiomatic: Chen took Zhong You as his model, Yue took Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive until each reached its utmost subtlety.

literal: Chen passed it to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;
idiomatic: Chen passed the art to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;

literal: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo.
idiomatic: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo — so the record runs.

literal: The craft was never broken through the generations.
idiomatic: The craft never failed from father to son.

literal: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were prized.
idiomatic: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were held in highest esteem.

literal: Xuanbo's running-draft script too was especially refined and ingenious, yet no traces survive.
idiomatic: Xuanbo's running-draft hand too was wrought to rare refinement, yet no trace of it remains.

literal: His son Hao inherited the title; he is treated in a separate biography.
idiomatic: His son Hao inherited the title and has a separate biography.

literal: The second son Jian, courtesy name Chongliang, [5] also called Lan.
idiomatic: The second son, Jian, courtesy name Chongliang,[5] was also called Lan.

literal: He loved learning and in youth was famed for fine calligraphy.
idiomatic: He loved learning and in youth was famed for fine calligraphy — so the record runs.

literal: At the beginning of the Founding Emperor's reign, [6] he rose through posts to Secretariat Gentleman, General Who Campaigns the Barbarians, Five-Rank Marquis, and participated in compiling the dynastic record.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Founding Emperor's reign[6] he rose step by step to secretariat gentleman, general who campaigns the barbarians, five-rank marquis, and a post compiling the dynastic record.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: Jian's younger brother Tian, courtesy name Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Tian, courtesy name Shuxuan, childhood name Bai — so the record runs.

literal: He rose through attendant at court audience and was granted the title Baron of Yimu.
idiomatic: He rose through attendant at court audience and was granted the title baron of Yimu.

literal: He went out as Administrator of Shangdang, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Shangdang, general who pacifies the south, and inspector of Yuzhou.

literal: He was advanced to Marquis of Yangwu.
idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Yangwu.

literal: He was executed on account of Hao's crime.
idiomatic: He was executed when Hao fell.

literal: At first, because of the turmoil of Fu Jian, Xuanbo wished to flee south to the Yangtze; on Mount Tai he was seized by Zhang Yuan — his plan failed, so he wrote a poem to wound himself, yet did not circulate it in his time, fearing guilt.
idiomatic: Early on, in the chaos of Fu Jian's fall, Xuanbo meant to flee south across the Yangtze; on Mount Tai Zhang Yuan seized him. The plan failed, and he wrote a poem to grieve himself, yet dared not let it circulate, fearing blame.

literal: When Hao was executed, Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun received an edict to seize Hao's household and first saw this poem.
idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, secretariat gentleman Gao Yun, ordered to seize Hao's household, first saw this poem.

literal: Yun understood its intent; Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.
idiomatic: Yun knew what it meant; Yun's grandson Chuo copied it into Yun's collected works.

literal: At first Xuanbo's uncle Qian had written the draft eulogy for his brother Hun in his own hand; [7] in the beginning of the Yanchang era, Assistant in the Office for Compiling the Dynastic Record Wang Zunye bought books in the market and came upon it.
idiomatic: Long before, Xuanbo's uncle Qian had penned in his own hand the draft eulogy for his brother Hun;[7] at the opening of the Yanchang era, assistant in the office for compiling the dynastic record Wang Zunye bought books in the market and found it.

literal: Counting from the eulogy to the present, nearly two hundred years had passed; he treasured the writing and kept it hidden deep.
idiomatic: Nearly two hundred years had passed since the eulogy was written; he treasured the script and hid it away.

literal: In the Wuding era, Zunye's son Songnian gave it to Attendant at the Yellow Gate Cui Jishu, and many copied it.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era Zunye's son Songnian gave it to attendant at the yellow gate Cui Jishu, and many took copies.

literal: Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall Yao Yuanbiao, famed in the time for skill in calligraphy, saw Qian's writing and said it surpassed his own.
idiomatic: Left grand master of the bright hall Yao Yuanbiao, famed in his day for calligraphy, saw Qian's hand and said it surpassed his own.

literal: Xuanbo's younger brother Hui, courtesy name Xuanyou.
idiomatic: Xuanbo's younger brother Hui, courtesy name Xuanyou — so the record runs.

literal: In youth he had literary talent and was famed together with Bohai Gao Yan.
idiomatic: In youth he had literary gift and shared renown with Bohai's Gao Yan.

literal: At first he was summoned as Vice Prefect of Xiangzhou and Secretariat Gentleman; he was gradually moved to Director of the Secretariat, granted Marquis of Beiqiu, and made Dragon-Charging General.
idiomatic: At first he was summoned as vice prefect of Xiangzhou and secretariat gentleman; he rose by degrees to director of the secretariat, was granted marquis of Beiqiu, and made dragon-charging general.

literal: Prince of Le'an Fan was stationed at Chang'an; Emperor Shizu, because Fan was young and the people of the three Qin — Han and alien alike — relied on perilous terrain and were prone to change, chose men of old loyalty and clear virtue to guard with him.
idiomatic: Prince of Le'an Fan held Chang'an; Emperor Shizu, seeing Fan was young and that Han and alien alike in the three Qin leaned on rough country and were quick to turn, chose men of old loyalty and clear virtue to stand guard with him.

literal: Hui was made Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, overseer of military affairs of Yong, Jing, Liang, and Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, deputy commander, acting Tutor to the Prince of Le'an, and advanced to Duke of Jinan.
idiomatic: Hui was made regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, overseer of military affairs in Yong, Jing, Liang, and Qin, general who pacifies the west, deputy commander, acting tutor to the prince of Le'an, and raised to duke of Jinan.

literal: In government he kept to the great outline and did not busy himself with small matters.
idiomatic: In office he kept to the great outline and did not fuss over small things.

literal: By nature he loved human relations.
idiomatic: By nature he loved the weave of human ties.

literal: Receiving guests he might speak of days gone by or discourse on right conduct, instructing the young — all day without cease.
idiomatic: When he received guests he might speak of days gone by or argue the way of right, guiding the young without cease from dawn to dusk.

literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to the capital.
idiomatic: Illness summoned him back to the capital.

literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhenjun, posthumously titled Duke Yuan.
idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenjun and was posthumously titled Duke Yuan.

literal: Men of standing all sighed in regret.
idiomatic: Men of standing all sighed for him.

literal: At that time Cui Kuan of Qinghe, courtesy name Jingren.
idiomatic: At that time Cui Kuan of Qinghe, courtesy name Jingren — so the record runs.

literal: His grandfather Tong, following Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao, fled to Longyou and then served Juqu and Li Gao.
idiomatic: His grandfather Tong, following Jin's Prince of Nanyang Bao, fled to Longyou and then served Juqu and Li Gao — so the record runs.

literal: His father Pou, courtesy name Bozong, was often ardent with longing for the eastern lands and would sigh: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows unceasing — that is what I hope for.
idiomatic: His father Pou, courtesy name Bozong, burned with longing for the eastern lands and often sighed: "Wind and rain dark, the cock crows without cease — that is what I hope for.

literal: " When Emperor Shizu toured west, Pou gathered those of shared intent and sent Kuan to submit allegiance.
idiomatic: " When Emperor Shizu toured west, Pou gathered men of shared intent and sent Kuan to offer allegiance.

literal: The emperor commended this, made Kuan General of Awesome Distance, Magistrate of Qiyang, and granted him Baron of Yishui.
idiomatic: The emperor commended him, made Kuan general of awesome distance and magistrate of Qiyang, and granted him baron of Yishui.

literal: He sent an envoy to go west with Kuan and soothe the newly submitted.
idiomatic: He sent an envoy west with Kuan to soothe the newly submitted.

literal: Pou was summoned to the capital but fell ill and died before he arrived.
idiomatic: Pou was summoned to the capital but fell ill and died on the road.

literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Pou's loyalty had shown in the former court, posthumously made him Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, General Who Stabilizes the West, Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Wuling, posthumous title Yuan.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, because Pou's loyalty had shone in the former reign, posthumously made him regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, general who stabilizes the west, inspector of Liangzhou, duke of Wuling, with posthumous title Yuan.

literal: Kuan returned to court and was made Secretariat Gentleman, General Who Pacifies the North, and Baron of Anguo.
idiomatic: Kuan returned to court as secretariat gentleman, general who pacifies the north, and baron of Anguo.

literal: Before long he went out as Administrator of Hongnong.
idiomatic: Before long he went out as administrator of Hongnong.

literal: When Kuan first submitted allegiance he met Minister of Works Hao.
idiomatic: When Kuan first offered allegiance he met minister of works Cui Hao.

literal: Hao was near him in age and treated him with deep kindness.
idiomatic: Hao was near his age and treated him with deep kindness.

literal: When Hao was executed, as a distant kinsman who had come from afar he alone was not implicated.
idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, as a distant kinsman newly come from the west he alone escaped punishment.

literal: He then made his home in Wucheng, dwelling on the old site of the Minister of Works' grove, and had one son inherit the wife of Hao's younger brother Lan, nee Feng, [8] — they supported one another as kin.
idiomatic: He then settled in Wucheng on the old grove of the minister of works and had one son take as wife Hao's younger brother Lan's widow, nee Feng,[8] tending one another as kin.

literal: Later Kuan inherited the title Duke of Wuling and General Who Stabilizes the West and was made garrison commander of Shancheng.
idiomatic: Later Kuan inherited duke of Wuling and general who stabilizes the west and was made garrison commander of Shancheng.

literal: The land of the two Xiao passes was perilous; [9] the people were much given to robbery.
idiomatic: The two Xiao passes were steep country;[9] the people were much given to robbery.

literal: Kuan was by nature witty; he drew in local magnates and chiefs of old bandits, befriended them, poured out his heart in treating them, and did not reject even small matters.
idiomatic: Kuan was witty by nature; he drew in local magnates and chiefs of old bandit bands, befriended them, poured out his heart, and did not spurn even small courtesies.

literal: Thus he could win the people's glad hearts — none failed to be moved by his spirit.
idiomatic: Thus he won the people's glad hearts, and none failed to answer his spirit.

literal: At the time officials had no salary allotment and took their supply only from the people.
idiomatic: At the time officials had no salary and lived only on what the people gave.

literal: Kuan was skilled at soothing and drawing them in, inviting gifts of courtesy — he received much, yet those who gave bore no resentment.
idiomatic: Kuan was skilled at soothing them and drawing gifts of courtesy; he took much, yet those who gave bore no grudge.

literal: Moreover Hongnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber, and the roads ran south in trade.
idiomatic: Moreover Hongnong was rich in lacquer, wax, bamboo, and timber, and the roads ran south with merchants.

literal: His household grew wealthy, yet the common people were glad of it.
idiomatic: His house grew rich, yet the common people were glad of it.

literal: Among the garrisons he was called able in government.
idiomatic: Among the garrisons he was called able in government — so the record runs.

literal: When he left the garrison and returned to the capital, many people followed in longing; more than three hundred went to the palace gates with memorials.
idiomatic: When he left the garrison for the capital, many followed in longing, and more than three hundred brought memorials to the palace gates.

literal: When the memorials were submitted, Emperor Gaozu commended him.
idiomatic: When the memorials were read, Emperor Gaozu commended him.

literal: He died in the second year of Yanxing, aged sixty-three; he left orders for a plain burial, enshrouded in daily dress.
idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yanxing, aged sixty-three, leaving orders for a plain burial in the clothes he wore day to day.

literal: His eldest son Chang, courtesy name Gongshi, inherited the title; by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: His eldest son Chang, courtesy name Gongshi, inherited the title; by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis — so the record runs.

literal: From Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Masters of Writing he went out as Chancellor of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: From attendant-in-ordinary of the masters of writing he went out as chancellor of Pingyuan.

literal: Chang was by nature harsh and impatient; he and Inspector Yang Chun repeatedly memorialized against each other, and Chang was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Chang was harsh and impatient; he and inspector Yang Chun repeatedly denounced each other in memorials, and Chang was dismissed.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made Administrator of Julu.
idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made administrator of Julu.

literal: When his younger brother Fei rebelled, Chang was hidden by Huangmu Army Commander Han Wenshu.
idiomatic: When his younger brother Fei rebelled, Chang was hidden by Huangmu army commander Han Wenshu.

literal: His whole household was registered and confiscated; only Chang's wife, Lady Li, as a princess's niece, kept with her two hundred-odd slaves, fields, and houses and was spared.
idiomatic: His whole household was registered and seized; only Chang's wife, Lady Li, as a princess's niece, kept two hundred-odd slaves with their fields and houses and was spared.

literal: In the Zhenguang era a general pardon lifted the ban; Chang recovered the title Marquis of Qijun and was made Dragon-Charging General and Palace Scribe.
idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era a general pardon lifted the ban; Chang recovered marquis of Qijun and was made dragon-charging general and palace scribe.

literal: In the Xiaochang era he was Administrator of Zhao.
idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he was administrator of Zhao commandery.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: Chang's younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Gonglu, was a court gentleman in attendance.
idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Gonglu, was a court gentleman in attendance — so the record runs.

literal: When Fei rebelled, because he had been given in adoption to another line he was pardoned.
idiomatic: When Fei rebelled, because he had been given in adoption to another line he was pardoned — so the record runs.

literal: He rose through Secretariat Gentleman, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Chief Rectifier of Jizhou.
idiomatic: He rose through secretariat gentleman, erudite of the imperial academy, right chief clerk of the ministry of personnel, general who campaigns north, grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon, and chief rectifier of Jizhou.

literal: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his goods and accused Chang's sons Ji and two others of not being his brother's seed; the suit dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.
idiomatic: After Chang died, Zhong coveted his goods and accused Chang's sons Ji and two others of not being his brother's blood; the suit dragged on for years, and gentlemen despised him.

literal: Erzhu Shilong as Director of the Masters of Writing memorialized to strip him of office — barred for life from the rolls.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, as director of the masters of writing, memorialized to strip him of office and bar him for life from the rolls.

literal: Fei loved learning and had literary talent.
idiomatic: Fei loved learning and had literary gift.

literal: He rose through Supervising Secretary and Recorder under Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
idiomatic: He rose through supervising secretary and recorder under Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

literal: He joined Yu in rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: He joined Yu in rebellion and was executed — so the record runs.

literal: Heng's younger brother Shu was a Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: Heng's younger brother Shu was a secretariat gentleman.

literal: There was also Cui Mo, courtesy name Sifan, descendant of Wei's Commandant of the Capital Cui Yan's elder brother Ba.
idiomatic: There was also Cui Mo, courtesy name Sifan, descended from Wei's commandant of the capital Cui Yan's elder brother Ba.

literal: His father Zun was Junior Chamberlain under Murong Chui.
idiomatic: His father Zun was junior chamberlain under Murong Chui.

literal: His uncle Zheng was Administrator of Guangchuan.
idiomatic: His uncle Zheng was administrator of Guangchuan.

literal: Mo, at the end of Murong Xi's reign, crossed south of the Yellow River and served Liu Yu as Administrator of Xingyang, garrisoning Hulao.
idiomatic: Mo, at the end of Murong Xi's reign, crossed south of the Yellow River and served Liu Yu as administrator of Xingyang, garrisoning Hulao.

literal: In the Shenqi era Pingtai was pacified and Mo surrendered.
idiomatic: In the Shenqi era Pingtai was pacified and Mo surrendered — so the record runs.

literal: Later he was granted Baron of Wuling and made General Who Extends Far.
idiomatic: Later he was granted baron of Wuling and made general who extends far.

literal: At first, while Mo was in the south, his wife Lady Zhang had two sons, Chongzhi and Jirou.
idiomatic: At first, while Mo was in the south, his wife Lady Zhang bore two sons, Chongzhi and Jirou.

literal: When Mo reached the capital he was given Lady Jin as wife and she bore a son, Youdu.
idiomatic: When Mo reached the capital he was given Lady Jin as wife, and she bore a son, Youdu.

literal: Chongzhi and the others, because their father was far away, gathered goods and, through intermediaries at the border, plotted to ransom Mo home.
idiomatic: Chongzhi and the others, their father far away, gathered goods and through men at the border plotted to ransom Mo home.

literal: Their mother Lady Zhang would often say to them: "Your father's nature is timid at heart and by origin lacks resolve — he will surely not come.
idiomatic: Their mother Lady Zhang would often tell them: "Your father's heart is timid and by nature he lacks resolve — he will surely not come."
